path: Motion, ASCII and particles. Everything here moves, so every component takes its frames from lib/loop.ts, extends MotionProps, and draws the same pixels for the same seed and time. The ASCII set follows published algorithms and credits the paper rather than the site it was found through. The particle set is originated: STYLE.md permits a seeded particle system and still forbids sparkle and confetti, so each one draws structure rather than decoration, takes its colors from the palette, and never glows or blends additively. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Ticker Tape
components.brief: A continuous horizontal ticker generated from JSON items shaped as [{ label, value }]. The props interface extends MotionProps. The core joins one logical cycle into a mono text track, repeats that track inside its own aria-hidden layer until two host widths are covered, and moves the layer left or right by a measured cycle width. A visually hidden copy contains each item once in source order. This is distinct from marquee because ticker-tape owns flat JSON text and its separators, has no children or MutationObserver, and creates no focus or hover behavior. Marquee wraps and moves arbitrary child elements while preserving their own semantics and interactions. Use animatedText from lib/a11y.ts, GRID_FONT from lib/font.ts, scope and styleHost from lib/host.ts, hashSeed from lib/rng.ts, and createLoop from lib/loop.ts. Seed chooses the starting item once with hashSeed(seed, 0), while time determines the subcycle offset. Randomness is never sampled per frame. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always draw the same text at the same pixel offset. The motion is slow enough to read, but the default speed must move the track about 38 pixels each second so the three second animation check is plainly visible. Measure the logical track, repeat it exactly, and wrap the offset modulo that measured width so there is no visible seam. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the time 1200 frame as one stationary track. At time 1200 with seed 1, the defaults show BUILD 184, VERIFY PASS, and SIZE 5.2 KB crossing the frame, with complete items on both sides. This is a good review frame because the data grammar, separator rhythm, fixed accent index mark, and seamless continuation are all visible at once. Look: one-pixel rules along the top and bottom, square corners, no shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corner, mono for every label and value, fg for primary text, muted for separators, and one stationary accent index mark at the leading edge. The accent never sets text. It has no disabled state because it is not a control, and it creates no focus target. Set meta.wave to 7, meta.facets to ["animated", "text"], meta.palette to ["fg", "accent", "muted"], meta.host to "div", and meta.stage to "fill". Defaults provide visible items, so do not set meta.demo. It is wrong if it accepts or clones children like marquee, if repeated accessible text is announced, or if the modulo reset exposes a jump or blank gap. The motion category budget is 6144 bytes minified and gzipped with shared runtime included. Expect about 4.1 KB. If it runs over, drop the seeded starting offset first and begin at item zero. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from seed through hashSeed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Count Up
components.brief: A single formatted number that advances from from to value and settles exactly on value. The props interface extends MotionProps. Use animatedText from lib/a11y.ts so assistive technology reads the final formatted number from the first frame while the changing visible layer is aria-hidden. Use GRID_FONT for the digits, styleHost for tabular figures, and createLoop from lib/loop.ts. Apply a fixed ease out quint curve over duration, round only after interpolation, clamp the last frame to value, and format prefix, decimals, grouping, and suffix consistently. This is distinct from odometer because count-up interpolates one numeric value and rewrites one text run. It does not model separate digit wheels or carries. There are no random choices, so seed is accepted through MotionProps but does not change the result. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always draw the same formatted number. The default changes by many readable increments during the first second, then slows visibly before settling without overshoot. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the final value immediately. At time 1200 the default has reached exactly 12,840 and the single accent bracket beside it is steady. This is a good review frame because the final grouping, tabular alignment, prefix and suffix spacing, and settled state can all be judged. Look: large mono tabular figures on the host background, a one-pixel muted baseline, one accent bracket at the start, square corners, and no shadow, glow, blur, rounded corner, or load transition. The accent is a mark, never text. It has no keyboard or pointer behavior, no disabled state, and no focus target. Set meta.wave to 7, meta.facets to ["animated", "text"], meta.palette to ["fg", "accent", "muted"], meta.host to "span", and meta.stage to "inline". Defaults already show a complete value, so do not set meta.demo. It is wrong if the final value remains one rounding step short, if proportional digits make the run jitter sideways, or if a screen reader hears every intermediate number. The motion category budget is 6144 bytes minified and gzipped with shared runtime included. Expect about 3.3 KB. If it runs over, drop configurable grouping first and keep plain deterministic formatting. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from seed through the approved runtime if randomness is ever added, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Split Flap
components.brief: A departure board whose logical cells flip through an allowed glyph alphabet until they reach the target rows from JSON. The props interface extends MotionProps. Draw it with createGrid from lib/glyph-grid.ts. Each logical flap occupies three grid columns and three grid rows. Box drawing glyphs make its square frame, the target or transient character sits in the center, and a horizontal hairline marks the hinge. The board is aria-hidden and a hiddenText node carries the final rows in reading order from the first frame. Use GRID_FONT, hiddenText, cssVar for palette color, hashSeed, and createLoop. For each target cell, hashSeed(seed, rowIndex, columnIndex) fixes its start delay and one or two extra alphabet steps. Compute its glyph from that fixed route and time. Never sample randomness per frame. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always draw the same glyph in every cell. The flip is represented by changing which glyph occupies a cell and by swapping upper and lower block marks. No glyph is translated, rotated, or scaled off the grid. At least one band of cells must visibly advance during every half second before the board settles. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the complete target board with every flap closed. At time 1200 and seed 1, the first row reads 09:20 SFO ON TIME, the third row is settled, and a diagonal band in the middle row is still resolving. This is a good review frame because most content is readable while the cell mechanism, seeded stagger, and single active accent hinge are visible. Look: fg glyphs, muted frames and secondary row labels, bg inside the flap faces, one accent hinge on the currently leading cell, one-pixel hairlines, square corners, mono throughout, and no shadow, glow, blur, rounded corner, or perspective transform. It has no keyboard or pointer behavior, no disabled state, and no focus target. Defaults contain three complete rows, so do not set meta.demo. It is wrong if cells spin independently without a readable seeded order, if characters leave the monospace grid, or if the 1200 frame is either illegible glyph soup or already entirely static. The motion category budget is 6144 bytes minified and gzipped with shared runtime included. Expect about 5.5 KB. If it runs over, drop the extra alphabet cycle and keep the seeded start delay. components.title: Odometer
components.brief: A bank of decimal wheels that rolls from one nonnegative integer to another. The props interface extends MotionProps. Draw it with createGrid from lib/glyph-grid.ts and use hiddenText from lib/a11y.ts for the final formatted value. Each logical wheel occupies one fixed column with its previous digit above in muted, its current digit on the center row in fg, and its next digit below in muted. Advance wheels by decimal carry order from right to left. A wheel changes only when the less significant wheels cross their carry boundary. This is distinct from count-up because odometer models separate digit wheels and carries on a cell grid. It never interpolates and rewrites one complete numeric string. Motion changes glyph occupancy between fixed rows. No digit is smoothly translated between cells. Use GRID_FONT, cssVar, createGrid, hiddenText, and createLoop. There are no random choices, so seed is accepted through MotionProps but does not alter the route. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always draw the same wheel states. The ease out timing slows the final carries, and the rightmost wheel must change several times in the first three seconds so the movement is unmistakable. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the final value with only the center row emphasized. At time 1200 the default has carried through 13000 while the last wheel is moving toward 2, with one accent carry marker above it. This is a good review frame because the destination is nearly readable and the mechanical difference from count-up is visible. Look: mono tabular figures, one-pixel upper and lower rules, square corners, fg current digits, muted neighboring digits, one accent carry marker, and no shadow, glow, blur, rounded corner, or perspective. The accent is a mark and never text. It has no keyboard or pointer behavior, no disabled state, and no focus target. Set meta.wave to 7, meta.facets to ["animated", "text"], meta.palette to ["fg", "accent", "muted"], meta.host to "span", and meta.stage to "inline". Defaults show a complete wheel bank, so do not set meta.demo. It is wrong if all digits crossfade together, if leading zero width changes the layout, or if a carry runs from left to right. components.title: Carousel
components.brief: A tabbed slide carousel over the host's direct children, following the Carousel pattern and Tabs pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide. The props interface extends MotionProps. Set meta.wraps to "panels". The core builds, before the panels, a rotation button, previous and next buttons, and a tablist with one tab per panel. The host has role region, aria-roledescription carousel, and an aria-label from label that does not repeat the word carousel. Direct children are tabpanels. The core may set only role, id, aria-labelledby, and hidden on them, restores those attributes on destroy, and reapplies them if React replaces a child. Hidden slides use the hidden attribute and are never merely placed offscreen. The rotation control is the first tab stop and its accessible label states the action, either Stop slide rotation or Start slide rotation. It does not use aria-pressed. The slide tabs name their panels, expose aria-selected and aria-controls, and use roving tabindex. Keyboard: Tab and Shift plus Tab follow the page sequence without custom interception. Enter or Space activates the focused rotation, previous, or next native button and focus stays on that button. On the tablist, Right Arrow and Left Arrow wrap through tabs with selection following focus, Home selects the first tab, End selects the last tab, and Tab leaves the tablist from its one active tab stop. Pointer: clicking rotation toggles automatic rotation, clicking previous or next selects the adjacent panel, and clicking a tab selects its panel. Hover pauses automatic movement while the pointer remains inside. Focus entering anywhere in the carousel stops rotation and it does not resume until the user activates the rotation control. Manual navigation never moves focus. The panels wrapper has aria-live off while rotation runs and polite while it is stopped, with aria-atomic false. Use native button elements, scope, hostAttributes, nextId, emitter, sameJson, and createLoop. It emits valueChange only from manual previous, next, or tab input, and rotationChange only from the rotation button. It is controlled through value, where null means uncontrolled, with defaultValue read once. Set meta.controlled to { value: "valueChange" }. The paused prop is an external hold. The rotation button maintains its own user requested rotation state without emitting during mount or update. There are no random choices, so seed is accepted through MotionProps but does not alter slide order. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always select the same automatic slide and progress position. Slide changes are instant. A one-pixel progress rule moves steadily enough to cover 20 percent of its track in the first 1200 milliseconds at the default interval, so animation is visibly changing within three seconds without moving the content itself. There is no visible loop seam when the last slide returns to the first because the progress rule resets exactly at a slide boundary. Under prefers-reduced-motion automatic rotation is off, the first slide is shown, the live region is polite, and all manual controls still work. At time 1200 the first default panel, Components drawn in text, is fully visible, all real controls are present, its first tab is selected, and the progress rule is one fifth complete. This is a good review frame because content, hierarchy, semantics, control states, and restrained motion can be judged together. Look: one-pixel hairlines, square corners, page font for panel prose and button labels, mono for slide numbers and the progress value, one accent rule under the selected tab, no pills, no shadow, glow, blur, rounded corner, or state transition. Hover adds at most a ten percent fg tint. Every native control gets a two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on focus-visible only. A previous or next button disabled by loop false sits at 45 percent opacity and remains visible. The accent never sets text. Set meta.wave to 7, meta.facets to ["animated", "interactive"], meta.palette to ["fg", "accent", "muted"], meta.host to "div", and meta.stage to "fill". Set meta.interactions to one list that tabs to the rotation button, presses Space, and expects rotationChange false, and a fresh list that clicks the next button, expects valueChange 1, and expects the second tab to have aria-selected true. Set meta.demo children to three article panels with headings Components drawn in text, One source, two shapes, and Motion you can pause, each followed by one short paragraph. It is wrong if rotation continues after focus enters, if hidden panels remain exposed or are only moved offscreen, or if previous and next are decorative glyphs instead of operable native buttons. The motion category budget is 6144 bytes minified and gzipped with shared runtime included. Expect about 5.9 KB. If it runs over, drop the visual progress rule first and retain every control, event, and accessibility behavior. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from seed through the approved runtime if randomness is ever added, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Stagger List
components.brief: The host's children appear in sequence through a restrained stagger. The props interface extends MotionProps. The core never moves, rewrites, removes, or changes attributes on a child. It uses scope from lib/host.ts to generate selectors for non-data-pica direct children, and a host custom property driven by createLoop controls each selector's opacity and vertical offset. A MutationObserver watches only the host child list, ignores the core's own nodes, and regenerates rules when the child count changes. The children remain in normal document order and in the accessibility tree throughout. Each item begins no more than distance pixels below its resting cell and reaches full opacity through a fixed ease out curve. It never uses visibility, hidden, display none, or an aria-hidden attribute on content. The core adds one aria-hidden accent rail and muted mono index ticks as its own data-pica layer, so the stagger reads as an ordered structure rather than a generic fade. There are no random choices, so seed is accepted through MotionProps but does not alter order. Pass paused, time, and fps to createLoop. Nothing else schedules a frame. The same seed and time always produce the same reveal fraction for each child. The default exposes a new item every 170 milliseconds and moves it eight pixels, so multiple items visibly change within the first three seconds. The reveal plays once and holds its completed state, so it has no loop seam. Under prefers-reduced-motion every child is fully visible at its final position and the rail remains static. At time 1200 all five demo items are visible and aligned, with the last item just settled. components.title: Flip Clock

Each flap occupies three grid columns and three rows, with box drawing sides, a horizontal hinge, an upper old half, and a lower new half during the first 260 milliseconds after a digit changes. Outside that window it shows one closed digit. The visible grid is aria-hidden and hiddenText carries the formatted time without a live region. Use GRID_FONT, cssVar, createGrid, hiddenText, and createLoop. There are no random choices, so seed is accepted through MotionProps but does not alter time or flap order. The seconds wheel changes once per second, with a clear upper to lower change during the flip, so visible motion occurs within three seconds. components.title: Infinite Columns
components.brief: Several vertical text columns scroll forever in alternating directions on a monospace cell grid. The props interface extends MotionProps. Input is JSON shaped as an array of string arrays, one array per column. Draw with createGrid from lib/glyph-grid.ts. Repeat each source array enough times to cover the grid, clip at the host edges, and compute every visible row by modular indexing. Even columns advance downward and odd columns advance upward. Motion changes which complete string occupies a row. Text never translates between rows or leaves the cell grid. A fixed accent hairline crosses the center row once, and muted box drawing rules separate columns, so the motion draws a legible table structure rather than decorative noise. The visible grid is aria-hidden. Give the host role img and an accessible label from label that names the moving column set without announcing repeated items. Use GRID_FONT, labelHost and unlabelHost, cssVar, createGrid, hashSeed, and createLoop. For each column, hashSeed(seed, columnIndex) selects one fixed starting row. Never sample randomness per frame. components.title: Particle Burst
components.brief: A pointer press emits a restrained radial particle burst from the pressed position. The particles draw a pressure diagram: a square centre mark, a dense expanding front, and short radial traces that reveal direction. They are not confetti, sparks, or a celebration. Pointerdown inside the host converts client coordinates to x and y fractions with x rightward and y downward, restarts the burst there, and captures no pointer because there is no drag. Pointer movement alone only updates the candidate origin. Pointerleave has no effect on an active burst. The host is not focusable and has no keyboard behavior because this is an optional decorative response that performs no action and communicates no state. For a finished default and capture, mount prepares one staged burst at the centre at time zero. Prepare seeded angles, radial ranks, speeds, drag, and trace lengths with createRng and hashSeed. A frame evaluates distance directly from burst age and the cached parameters, so it never integrates state, allocates particles, or reads the canvas back. A press changes only the normalized origin and start time, then reuses the arrays. The same seed, time, and normalized press produce the same pixels. There is no automatic repeating reset, so there is no loop seam. At defaults, the front moves at least 90px in the first three seconds. At time 1200 the staged burst occupies about one third of the shorter host side, with a dense square front, calm negative space, and the centre still visible. prefers-reduced-motion holds time 900 and ignores pointer animation, showing the compact pressure diagram as one static frame. components.title: Particle Trail
components.brief: A restrained particle trail follows the pointer and records its recent route as a pathline. Particles are ordered samples of motion with a clear head, taper, and age, so they draw trajectory and direction rather than sparkle around the cursor. Pointermove converts client coordinates to fractions of the host, with x increasing to the right and y increasing downward, and appends a point only after the pointer has moved a minimum distance. Pointerenter starts following. Pointerleave freezes the last target and lets the trail contract toward it. There is no click behavior. The host is not focusable and has no keyboard behavior because the trail is decorative and performs no action. Before the first pointer input, a seeded leader follows one slow closed S path so the default frame is complete. Prepare a fixed ring buffer, seeded lateral offsets, phase, and age ranks with createRng and hashSeed on mount and when seed, count, spread, or size changes. Pointer input updates coordinates in that fixed buffer but never allocates. Frames evaluate the cached path and decay directly from time. The default S path is periodic over 24000 ms with matched position and tangent, so it has no visible seam. After pointer input, the same seed, time, and normalized pointer history draw the same pixels. At defaults, the leader travels about 64px within three seconds and the tail visibly follows rather than sitting near the pointer. Time 1200 shows an S curve crossing the centre, with a compact head in the upper right and a long muted taper behind it. prefers-reduced-motion holds that time 1200 frame, ignores further pointer animation, and shows a static pathline. Use fg for the recent trail, muted for older samples, and one accent square for the leader. The accent never sets text.
